newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Saga 8-month pre-tax seen sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Saga 8-month pre-tax seen sharply higher.

text.p: Norway's largest independent oil company Saga Petroleum ASA is expected to record a profit before tax of 2.08 billion crowns for the first eight months of the year, a Reuter poll of eight analaysts showed.
The company booked a pre-tax profit of 1.2 billion crowns in the corresponding year-ago period.
Three of the analysts recommended a buy on the stock, three said hold, one said sell and one declined to provide a reccomendation.

Estimates of share's potential varied widely due to uncertainty surrounding oil prices. Most analysts were agreed oil prices would fall over the next two years, but forecasts for 1997 crude prices in 1997 varied by $3.5 dollars per barrel from $18 to $21.50.

One of the positive analysts saw a potential move upwards on the share price of 20 percent. Another projected a price of 120 crowns per share by the end of the year, increasing to between 140 and 150 crowns during 1997.
On Friday Saga's A share closed at 105 crowns.
Saga will present results for the first eight months on October 3. Following lists analysts' estimates.
